transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... I guess what brings me in is just a little situation at work. It's really not a huge deal, I promise. I'm a personal care aide, and we had this staff meeting the other day. I just got really, I guess, passionate about what we were talking about? I got all worked up trying to show everyone this fall-prevention drill. I started moving the chairs around and waving my arms to demonstrate how to do it right... but I guess I got a bit carried away. I couldn't really seem to stop even when folks told me to sit down and take a breath. 

I was just trying to be helpful and make sure everyone was safe, you know? I didn't mean to cause a fuss. I hope that makes sense. Is it okay that I came in to talk to you about that?
Over the past few days, have you felt like you needed much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's actually been kind of nice, to be honest. I hope it's okay to say that. 

Like, lately I've only been sleeping maybe two or three hours... but I'll wake up way before dawn and I just feel completely rested and ready to go. I didn't really think anything was wrong with it, you know? I'll just be up making plans for the day while the house is still dark. It just feels like I'm getting a good head start on things so I can be more prepared. That's not a bad thing, right?
Before this started happening, have you ever had periods in your life where you felt very down, sad, or lacked energy for weeks at a time?

Um, no... I don't really think so. I mean, everybody has a bad day here and there, right? But nothing like what you're saying, where I'm just down and out for weeks. I try to stay pretty upbeat, especially for my clients. They need me to be positive, so I just try to keep a smile on my face. I hope that's the right answer... I just haven't really felt sad like that.
Aside from this recent time, have you ever had other periods in your life where you felt this unusually energetic, keyed up, or needed very little sleep?

Well, um... I guess maybe this isn't the very first time. I hope you aren't disappointed in me for not mentioning it right away. 

It's just that... well, for about the last 11 months or so, I've had these stretches where I get really energized and I don't need much sleep, and I start making all these big plans. It kind of comes and goes. But I always thought I was just being really productive, you know? Like I was just doing a really good job at work and getting things done around the house. I really try my best to be helpful. 

Is it bad that this has been happening on and off for almost a year? I promise I haven't been trying to cause any trouble with it.
During these times when you feel so energized, do your thoughts seem to race or jump very quickly from one idea to another?

Um, well... I guess maybe my thoughts do move a little fast sometimes? But I always just thought it meant I had a lot of good ideas all at once. That's a sign of a sharp mind, isn't it? 

Like, I'll be thinking about my clients at work, and then suddenly I'm thinking about church, and then my wife, and then I'll get this great idea for a new workshop... and it just goes so quick. Sometimes I actually lose the first thought before I can even say it out loud because the next one is already there. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound scattered or anything. I really do try to stay focused. It's just that my brain is working so hard to keep up with everything I want to do. Is it okay that my mind works like that?
Between those energized stretches over the last 11 months, did your mood and energy return completely back to normal?

Um... well, mostly? I mean, my energy definitely went back to normal. There was a stretch in between where I was sleeping fine again, and I wasn't rushing around trying to do a million projects at once. I was just, you know, being regular me. 

But... I hope this doesn't sound too strange, and I really hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying this... but even when my energy was back to normal for those few weeks, I still had some other things going on. Like, I would still hear someone calling my name when no one was there. And... well, I was still pretty sure that people at work were taking notes on me. 

I tried not to let it bother me, and I kept doing my job the best I could. I really hope that's okay. Does that make sense, that I'd be calm but still having those things happen?
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, or other recreational drugs during these past 11 months?

Oh, no. No, sir. I... I really try to take good care of myself, you know? I don't drink or use any kind of drugs at all. I know those things aren't good for you, and I wouldn't want to do anything to mess up my health or my job. 

I really try to be a good person and do the right thing. I hope you believe me. I wouldn't lie to you about something like that. Is it okay that I just stick to water and coffee?
